title: Decap candidate selection fork: C evicts expired during scan, Python/Rust select-longest-then-expire
description: Three-way parity drift in tunnel-auth decap candidate selection, corpus-invisible (found by kimi-k3 correctness review of b7z9.93). With an expired LONGEST-prefix grant and a live SHORTER grant over the same route_hash: Python (tunnel_auth.py:545-555) and Rust (lichen-gateway/src/tunnel_auth.rs authorize_decapsulation, pinned by expired_longest_prefix_denies_without_falling_back_to_shorter_live_grant) select the longest candidate including expired ones and deny EXPIRED; C (lichen/subsys/lichen/gateway/tunnel_auth.c:468-474) evicts expired candidates during the scan and PERMITS via the live shorter grant - pinned deliberately by test_decap_expired_shadow (lichen/tests/tunnel_auth/src/main.c:219-261, commit 7e39bf4655 'decap skips expired grants, keeps EXPIRED'). All three suites pass because test/vectors/tunnel_authorization.json has no mixed expired-longest/live-shorter decap case. Needs adjudication: either (a) C semantics win - align Python+Rust and keep them permitted-by-shorter, or (b) Python/Rust semantics win - revert C to select-then-expiry and update 7e39bf4655's test, plus in BOTH cases add a shared corpus decap case (e.g. expired_at_boundary_longest_live_shorter) so the fork cannot reappear silently. Do NOT just pick one side silently; the 7e39bf4655 resolution and the Python-parity comments (tunnel_auth.rs:420-424 'Python parity') contradict each other, which is exactly why this needs a decision.
